$comment: THE ARTIFACT TYPE CATALOG. Single source of truth. See storyArtifactTypes.ts for why this is a JSON file in git and not 11 rows in artifact_definitions. Add a type by adding an entry here; the tests derive their expectations from this file, so nothing else needs editing to stay honest. file_types are lowercase extensions WITHOUT a dot; ["*"] means any extension. evidence_source: 'repo' the git tree is the evidence, 'platform' an upload recorded against the story is the evidence, 'either' both are accepted and the contract entry may name which. requires_github_validation MUST equal (evidence_source === 'repo'); the invariant is asserted by a test rather than trusted.

types.name: Case study
types.evaluation_criteria: A reader outside the project can say what the problem was, what was built, and what changed as a result, without asking the builder a question.
types.exists_today: 191 runtime_portfolio_artifacts rows of this kind plus 205 in case_study_artifacts

types.name: Proposal
types.evaluation_criteria: States the scope, the price and the dates a client would sign against, and every requirement it claims to answer is cited rather than asserted.
types.exists_today: Proposal Studio and the gov build track both already produce these

types.name: Portfolio entry
types.evaluation_criteria: Shows the work to someone deciding whether to hire the builder, and survives being read with no narration.
types.exists_today: runtime_portfolio_artifacts, and the viewer is already built

types.name: Build artifact
types.evaluation_criteria: The thing the story said would exist, in the repo, at the commit that produced it, with a capture showing it running.
types.exists_today: 299 rows, 233 of them carrying a commit sha

types.name: Analysis report
types.evaluation_criteria: A reader who has never seen the project can say what was predicted or measured, how well, and against what baseline.
types.exists_today: Nothing. This is the gap the churn boards show.

types.name: Data workbook
types.evaluation_criteria: Every column is named in a way a stranger can read, and every derived number can be traced to the input it came from.
types.exists_today: The platform viewer already supports both formats

types.name: Architecture decision record
types.evaluation_criteria: Names the decision, the options rejected and the reason, so the next person does not reopen it from scratch.

types.name: Field guide
types.evaluation_criteria: Someone doing the task for the first time can follow it without the author present.

types.name: Prompt library
types.evaluation_criteria: Each prompt says what it is for and what good output looks like, so it can be reused rather than rewritten.

types.name: Demo capture
types.evaluation_criteria: Shows the feature actually running, in the deployed demo rather than on the builder's machine.
types.exists_today: The capture work on the gov track produces these but never uploads them

types.name: Presentation
types.evaluation_criteria: Stands on its own in the room it was built for, and makes one claim per slide that the artifacts behind it can support.
